reproduction_target: Computational reproduction of the plasmid Fiber-seq analyses: PacBio HiFi read alignment to a combined linearized-plasmid + hg38 reference (pbmm2/minimap2), m6A/nucleosome footprint calling (fibertools-rs) and CpG methylation (jasmine), full-length-fiber filtering, FIRE regulatory-element calling on genomic samples, FiberHMM sub-nucleosomal footprint calling, plasmid-vs-genomic nucleosome-density comparison, lowly/intermediately/highly chromatinized read categorization, ENCODE CTCF/DNase footprint comparison for genomic promoters, and the LDLR MPRA subsample/z-score/BH-FDR statistical analysis (author fiberseq_MPRA package).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods (Fiber-seq Data Processing; Comparison of plasmid and genomic nucleosome density; Categorization; Encode tracks; LDLR MPRA Statistical analysis; Code Availability). Author repo github.com/StergachisLab/Plasmid-Fiber-seq is thin ('Scripts and data' + wiki) and ships conda env EXPORTS (environments/plasmid_fiberseq.yml, environments/FiberHMM.yml) with full package=version=build strings, plus the fiberseq_MPRA_package Python package and a small LDLR test-data subset; repo/wiki not read at line level (stage-1 prose-only). No Data Availability statement and NO GEO/SRA/ENA accession for the study's own PacBio Fiber-seq data. Wet-lab plasmid/cell/library generation counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Read alignment of plasmid Fiber-seq HiFi reads to a combined linearized-plasmid + hg38 reference (pbmm2 1.14.99 / minimap2 2.28 pinned in environments/plasmid_fiberseq.yml; aligner not named in prose)
m6A methylation & nucleosome footprint identification (fibertools-rs) + CpG methylation calling (jasmine, PacBio) — no versions in prose; not covered by shipped conda env exports
Full-length fiber filtering (reference length +/-50 bp, >=10% m6A methylation) for downstream plasmid analysis
FIRE (Fiber-seq Inferred Regulatory Elements) calling on genomic samples via the FIRE pipeline (ref 39) — no version in prose; not in shipped env exports
FiberHMM sub-nucleosomal footprint calling on plasmid samples (ref 21; environments/FiberHMM.yml conda export ships hmmlearn 0.2.5 etc.)
Plasmid-vs-genomic nucleosome-density comparison (fibertools-rs nucleosome footprints; genomic fibers length-matched +/-50 bp, >=2 FIRE peaks)
Categorization of lowly/intermediately/highly chromatinized reads (benchmark slope 0.005 nucleosomes/bp; <20% = lowly, >60% = highly)
ENCODE CTCF/DNase footprint comparison for genomic promoters (CTCF ChIP-seq HEK293 ENCSR000DTW; DNase-seq HEK293T ENCSR000EJR)
LDLR MPRA statistical analysis (author fiberseq_MPRA package + FiberHMM): 5,000-read subsamples x10,000, WT-vs-variant footprint-occupancy z-scores, one-tailed p, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 5%

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Only 2/9 computational steps (C8 ENCODE public-reuse comparison; C9 LDLR MPRA statistics, which ships an author package + small LDLR test subset) reach an RI ceiling at stage1. The other 7/9 steps (C1-C7: alignment, methylation/footprint calling, filtering, FIRE, FiberHMM, density comparison, categorization) cap at X because the study publishes NO Data Availability statement and NO GEO/SRA/ENA accession for its own PacBio Fiber-seq reads or processed fibers, and the plasmid reference sequences (Plasmidsaurus) are not deposited — so those steps cannot be run on the study's own data at all. The conda env exports (env_lock CLAIM, build-string level) do not cover fibertools-rs / jasmine / FIRE (unpinned). R* not assignable at stage1.
headline.coverage: 9 computational steps assessed from Methods prose + author repo landing/README/tree; 8 wet-lab plasmid/cell/library-generation procedures counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope.

gaps.where: Study's own primary data: PacBio Revio plasmid Fiber-seq reads and all downstream processed fibers (m6A/nucleosome/CpG calls, FiberHMM footprints, LDLR MPRA full read pool of 291,888 WT reads)
gaps.missing: There is NO Data Availability statement and NO GEO/SRA/ENA/Zenodo accession anywhere in the paper for the study's own sequencing data. Only a small LDLR footprint test subset is bundled in the code repo; the full raw/processed datasets are not publicly downloadable, so nearly all computational steps cannot be executed on the study's own data.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a Data Availability statement and deposit raw HiFi reads (SRA/ENA) plus processed Fiber-seq outputs (GEO/Zenodo) with a sample-to-figure manifest.

gaps.missing: Reference sequences were obtained from Plasmidsaurus whole-plasmid Nanopore sequencing with 'custom analysis and annotation'; the linearized plasmid references (a required alignment input) are not deposited or described in reproducible detail.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the final linearized plasmid reference FASTA(s) and the combined plasmid+hg38 reference used for alignment.

gaps.missing: The repo ships conda env EXPORTS (environments/plasmid_fiberseq.yml, environments/FiberHMM.yml) with full package=version=build strings — a strong env_lock CLAIM (unvalidated at stage1, no OS/platform closure, no container digest). However fibertools-rs, jasmine (PacBio), and the FIRE pipeline are NOT covered by these exports and carry no version in prose (unpinned).
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a resolvable lock (conda-lock/pixi.lock) or container digest that also pins fibertools-rs, jasmine, and FIRE; declare target OS/platform.

gaps.missing: Code Availability names github.com/StergachisLab/Plasmid-Fiber-seq, but the README is one line ('Scripts and data', pointing to a wiki). The fiberseq_MPRA_package is present, but the end-to-end figure-reproduction glue (alignment invocation, filtering, density comparison, categorization) is not evidently versioned/tagged and lives partly in the wiki (not read at stage1).
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release, add a README with run instructions mapping scripts to figures, and pin external-tool versions used by each script.

gaps.where: Wet-lab generation: plasmid construction, ER2796 transformation/extraction, HEK293/HEK293T culture, relaxed pEF-GFP generation, flow cytometry, plasmid Fiber-seq (m6A-MTase) reactions, PacBio SMRTbell library prep + Revio sequencing, LDLR MPRA library bottleneck/transfection
gaps.missing: Wet-lab steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted.
